title: Labour market effects of COVID-19 in sub-Saharan Africa: an informality lens from Burkina Faso, Mali and Senegal
summary: Using real-time survey evidence from Burkina Faso, Mali and Senegal, the paper shows that workers in the informal economy were hit harder by the COVID-19 pandemic. Informal workers were more likely to lose their jobs, see earnings fall and struggle to meet basic needs.
keyFindings: Informal workers were more likely to lose their jobs and see their earnings fall.
Informal workers were more likely to struggle to meet basic needs during the pandemic.
Remittances from family members helped soften the adverse effects.
methods: Survey of 900 individuals in Burkina Faso, Mali and Senegal, collected 20 April–1 May 2020 during lockdowns.
